title: Why most algo traders blow up at month four
caption: Month four is the kill zone. Not because the strategy fails — because the trader does. Here's what survives, and what dies.

slides.headline: Why most algo traders blow up at
slides.sub: And the one rule that lets the rest survive.

slides.body:
Your strategy is fine. The backtest is fine.

What's not fine is what your hands do when you're three months into a drawdown and the bot just flagged another setup. That's where the equity curve dies.
Not because the edge disappeared — because position size got moved manually after 3 losing weeks.

slides.title: Pre-commit the rules in calm
slides.body: Decide entry, exit, sizing, and shutdown conditions when emotions are baseline. Write them down. Make them specific enough that no judgment call is required at decision time.

slides.title: The one-directional
slides.footer: Defense is automatic. Aggression is earned.

slides.quote: Discipline isn't a personality trait. It's an architecture choice.

slides.title: Track compliance, not perfection
slides.body: "Did I follow the rules today?" beats "did I win today?" Equity curve relative to expected drawdown range, never zero-drawdown. 28-of-30 success days, never 30-day streaks.
